diagnostic_evidence.quote: Differentiating the above expression and enforcing the correct asymptotic order of $\kappa_p'$ as $p\to p^\star$ proves that $M'=M$, yielding the first claim.
Note that $M$ distinct eigenvalue trajectories must be present near an order-$M$ bifurcation, e.g., by the fundamental theorem of algebra.
The claim then follows, once again, by comparing the derivative of the Puiseux series at $p=p^\star$ to the limit of the right-hand side of \cref{eq:bifurc_ord} as $p\to p^\star$.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof assumes that an order-$M'$ bifurcation (an $M'$-cycle of branches) always has Puiseux expansion with nonzero leading term $c(p-p^\star)^{1/M'}$. In general the leading exponent is $k/M'$ with $k\ge1$ (the cycle length is the lcm of all exponent denominators), so matching the blow-up rate of $\kappa_p'$ with $I$'s vanishing order only gives $k/M'=1/M$, i.e. $M'=kM$, not $M'=M$. E.g. a 4-cycle $\kappa^\star+c(p-p^\star)^{1/2}+c'(p-p^\star)^{3/4}$ satisfies the hypothesis $I=(p-p^\star)^{1/2}\widetilde I$ with $\widetilde I$ continuous nonzero, yet is not a quadratic bifurcation. The converse fails likewise: a cubic bifurcation $\kappa^\star+c(p-p^\star)^{2/3}$ gives $I\sim(p-p^\star)^{1/3}$, not $(p-p^\star)^{2/3}$, and $I$ is not $(\kappa_p-\kappa^\star)^{2}\overline I$; a bifurcation with leading integer term $(p-p^\star)+c(p-p^\star)^{3/2}$ has $I(p^\star)\ne0$. Both directions of the theorem rest on this unjustified step.

failure_location.quote: Namely, a \emph{Puiseux series} for $\kappa_p$ must exist: for some $M'\in\{2,3,\ldots\}$, and $c\in\mathbb{C}_{\neq0}$,

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add a hypothesis that the Puiseux expansion of $\kappa_p$ at $p^\star$ has nonzero coefficient at exponent $1/M'$ (generic case), or redefine 'order' via the leading fractional exponent, and restate the converse accordingly; adjust prop:disk:bifurc to 'at least cubic' unless the disk-specific $2\times2$ structure excludes higher cycles.
issues.overall_effect: The order-identification statements (both directions) in cor:bifurc_sufficient are unproven and false in degenerate Puiseux configurations; the 'precisely at a Bessel zero and is cubic' claim of prop:disk:bifurc (only 'order 3k' follows, and the Bessel-zero necessity uses the converse), the 'if and only if' bifurcation criterion after prop:annulus:bifurc_ord, and the remark rem:angle inherit the gap.
issues.title: Bifurcation order identified with Puiseux leading exponent without justification
issues.why_classification: A contained extra hypothesis or redefinition rescues a recognizably comparable theorem, but the converse and the exact-order claims as stated must be weakened and the proof supplemented.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: we observe that the indicator becomes positive if and only if an eigenvalue trajectory is (i) real and (ii) traveling to the right. Theory confirms this, since \cref{cor:bifurc} relates the sign of $\overline{I}$ to the sign of the derivative of a real trajectory.

issues.failure_explanation: With eq:ind_simpl and the disk formula, $\overline I(p)=J_m(\kappa_p)^2\ge0$, contradicting the claim that $\overline I$ is strictly negative for real disk trajectories (and the table's $\overline I\sim-|p-p^\star|^\alpha$). Moreover, by eq:bifurc_ord with $n_p'=2p>0$, $\kappa_p>0$, sign$\,\kappa_p'=$ sign$\,I$, and for $p>1$ eq:ind_simpl gives sign$\,\overline I=-$sign$\,I$; hence theory gives $\overline I>0$ iff the real trajectory travels left, the opposite of the asserted 'positive iff traveling to the right'. The text's sign statements consistently correspond to $\overline I=\frac{2}{a_m\pi(p^2-1)}I$, not to eq:ind_simpl (also the cited result should be lem:bifurc_ord, not cor:bifurc).

failure_location.quote: On the other hand, the indicator is strictly negative for real eigenvalue curves, except at bifurcation points, in agreement with \cref{cor:bifurc}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace $1-p^2$ by $p^2-1$ in eq:ind_simpl (and negate the formula in prop:annulus:bifurc_ord accordingly), or invert all sign statements about $\overline I$ in Sections 5 and 6, and cite lem:bifurc_ord for the sign relation.
issues.overall_effect: The sign-based interpretations of the indicator plots and the 'theory confirms' statement are inconsistent with the paper's own definitions; zero sets and bifurcation conclusions are unaffected.
issues.title: Sign of simplified indicator inconsistent between definition and stated sign claims
issues.why_classification: A local sign convention fix restores consistency without altering any substantive result.

issues.title: Annulus indicator formula derived only for real eigenvalues but stated without realness
issues.why_classification: Adding the standard realness hypothesis is a local fix that preserves all uses of the result.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: a real (piecewise-smooth) eigenvalue trajectory undergoes bifurcation if and only if $\|v_p\|_{L^\infty(\partial B_1)}=r\|v_p\|_{L^\infty(\partial B_r)}$

issues.failure_explanation: With $v_p=A_\rho\phi(m\theta)$ on $\partial B_\rho$ and arc-length measure $\rho\,d\theta$, $\|v_p\|^2_{L^2(\partial B_r)}=r|A_r|^2a_m\pi$ and $\|v_p\|^2_{L^2(\partial B_1)}=|A_1|^2a_m\pi$. Equality of the $L^2$ norms means $|A_1|=\sqrt r|A_r|$, whereas the sup-norm condition is $|A_1|=r|A_r|$. The two conditions are not equivalent for $0<r<1$.

failure_location.quote: By the assumed polar-coordinate separability in \cref{eq:annulus:functions}, this is actually equivalent to $\|v_p\|_{L^2(\partial B_1)}=\|v_p\|_{L^2(\partial B_r)}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the equivalence by $\|v_p\|_{L^2(\partial B_1)}=\sqrt r\,\|v_p\|_{L^2(\partial B_r)}$ (or delete the sentence).
issues.overall_effect: The restated $L^2$ criterion for annulus bifurcations is wrong by a factor $\sqrt r$; the sup-norm criterion itself is unaffected and the $L^2$ version is not used elsewhere.
issues.title: Incorrect equivalence between boundary sup-norm and L^2-norm bifurcation conditions
issues.why_classification: A one-line correction of an unused restatement; no result depends on it.
